My land is in the flat fields east of town, maybe 8 mu total. My husband's parents farmed it before us, and I've worked this same ground for over thirty years. I know what grows here.

Wheat in winter, corn in summer. That's what I do. That's what my neighbors do. The grain station in town buys both, so I know I'll have somewhere to sell. I can't afford to try something new and have it fail — I don't have extra money sitting around.

For wheat, I'll plant in mid-October like always. I'll buy the improved seed from the village cooperative store, same kind I've been getting the past few years. It does better than the old seed. Before I plant, I'll run the rotary tiller over the field to break up the hard soil after the corn. I water three times: once right after planting if the ground is too dry, once before winter sets in, and once when the wheat starts jointing in spring. I spray twice — once for weeds early on, once later if I see rust or powdery mildew. I put down the compound fertilizer and urea the way the fertilizer shop told me years ago.

For corn, I plant right after I harvest the wheat in June. I use hybrid seed — Zhengdan or whichever hybrid the shop has that year. I don't plow again, just plant directly into the stubble to save my back and save time. I only water if it doesn't rain at silking time in August. I put on one big dose of fertilizer, usually all at once when I plant.

I expect to get around 450 jin per mu of wheat and a bit more from the corn.
